title: From Ancient Herb to Nobel Prize: Artemisinin
description:
Ayurveda is often promoted as a safe and natural system of healing, but unlike modern medicine it still relies on outdated humoral theories and untested herbal concoctions. In this video, Pale Blue Thoughts explores the fascinating story of YouYou Tu, the Chinese scientist whose discovery of artemisinin transformed the fight against malaria and won her the 2015 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

We examine how Tu combined insights from traditional Chinese medicine with rigorous scientific research, randomized clinical trials, pharmacology, and evidence-based medicine to extract the key compound from Artemisia annua. Her work saved millions of lives and became a model of how plant-based medicine should be validated.

This video also takes a rational look at why Ayurveda causes drug-induced liver injury, how its pseudoscientific principles prevent real progress, and what Ayurveda would need to do to become truly scientific—discarding outdated slokas, isolating active ingredients, running safety studies, and adopting pharmacovigilance.

If you’ve searched for Ayurveda vs modern medicine, Ayurveda pseudoscience, YouYou Tu discovery, artemisinin malaria cure, Nobel Prize medicine, plant-based medicine, or traditional medicine myths, this video gives you the rational perspective.

Don’t forget to subscribe, like, comment, and share — hype this video so it reaches more people and sparks better conversations!

00:00 – Ayurveda vs modern medicine: why science matters
02:20 – Plant-based medicines that shaped modern medicine
05:00 – YouYou Tu: early life and inspiration
07:40 – Project 523 and the malaria crisis
11:30 – Discovery of Artemisinin and clinical trials
16:10 – Nobel Prize recognition and global impact
19:40 – Lessons for Ayurveda: evidence over tradition
